label: post-hoc (added 11/16 after the final run)
definition:
POST-HOC (added 11/16 after the final run; PI message 2026-11-16 ~02:35 KST). Outlier filter that does not condition on the
outcome period. Robustness only: no headline number and no pre-specified rule is changed; s04_analysis is imported, not modified.

Background. `s04_analysis.jumpy_buildings` (rows `imputation_drop_jumpy`, `imputation_health_drop_jumpy` of G7_imputation.csv; D21)
flags a building if ANY observed electricity month is > 3 x its own median or < median / 3, where both the median and the months
are taken over every observed month: pre-construction, construction and post-completion months (and, for control-pool buildings,
bulk-file months at or after their own start). A retrofit that lowers consumption, or a building emptied during the works, can
therefore put the building into the flagged set: the filter conditions on the outcome.

Here: the same rule (k = 3, own median, electricity, kWh > 0) on PRE months only
  treated buildings        months before the recorded construction start (phase == 'pre' in s04_analysis.load(): ym < start_ym)
  control-pool buildings   months before their own recorded start (same phase definition)
A building with no pre month is never flagged (as in the original rule a building without months is not flagged).
Then the headline imputation ATT is re-estimated without the flagged buildings, with the settings of `imputation_health_only`
(uses = health centres) and `imputation_use` (pooled): s04_analysis.imputation_did(fe='use', drop=flagged), IMP_NBOOT_HEAD
(default 1,000) bootstrap draws for both samples. For reference the original all-month rule is re-estimated with the same number
of draws (G7 holds it with IMP_NBOOT = 200 draws), and the unfiltered headline is copied from results/G7_imputation.json.

Decomposition of the original flags (headline treated buildings = treated buildings of the unfiltered headline sample):
offending months = months outside [median / 3, 3 x median] with the ALL-month median (the original rule), classified by phase.
  only_post            every offending month lies after completion
  only_constr          every offending month lies in the construction period
  only_constr_or_post  no offending month lies before the start (includes the two rows above and mixtures of them)
  any_pre              at least one offending month lies before the start
  not_flagged_by_pre_rule = flagged by the original rule but not by the pre-only rule (pre-only median); differs from
                            only_constr_or_post because the median changes when it is taken over pre months only.

Outputs: results/a_jump_pre.csv (one row per sample x filter), results/a_jump_pre.json (rows + counts + decomposition).
No network. About 3 minutes with 1,000 draws.

treated_flags.note: phases by the recorded dates: pre = before the start month, constr = start..completion month, post = after completion; offending months use the all-month median (original rule)
